questions.question: Mass movement is defined as:
options: The downslope movement of weathered material under GRAVITY, without a transporting agent such as a river, glacier or wind
Any material carried by a river

questions.question: A slope's resisting forces include:
options: Friction, interlocking particles, dry cohesion and plant ROOTS binding the soil

questions.question: Saturation destabilises a slope because water:
options: Fills the pores pushing particles apart, adds weight, and LUBRICATES potential slide surfaces

questions.question: Undercutting by a river, waves or a road cutting is dangerous because it:
options: Removes SUPPORT at the slope's base, exactly where resistance matters most

questions.question: Evidence of soil creep includes:
options: Tilted fence posts, curved tree trunks, terracettes, and soil piled against the upslope side of walls
A crescent scar and a back-tilted block
A valley filled with set mud
A fresh talus cone below a cliff

questions.question: Solifluction occurs when:
options: Dry sand avalanches down a dune
The thawed, waterlogged surface layer flows slowly over a FROZEN subsoil, as on the high Drakensberg and Lesotho slopes

questions.question: A slump differs from a landslide because the slump:
options: Moves along a perfectly flat plane
ROTATES along a curved, spoon-shaped surface, leaving a crescent scar and a tilted-back block

questions.question: The fastest, wettest and deadliest of the six movements is the:
options: MUD FLOW — saturated debris behaving as a fluid, racing down valleys and setting like concrete

questions.question: Environmental impacts of mass movement include:
options: Slopes stripped to bedrock, topsoil buried, and rivers choked with sediment that smothers aquatic life and silts dams

questions.question: In the April 2022 KwaZulu-Natal disaster:
options: Over 300 mm of rain fell in 24 hours, hillsides failed in hundreds of places, and more than 400 people died

questions.question: Poverty multiplies mass movement risk because:
options: Poor communities live only on flat land
Informal settlement is pushed onto steep, unstable slopes with cut platforms, leaking water and no engineering
Rainfall is heavier over poor areas

questions.question: Chapman's Peak Drive is a recurring example of:
options: ROCK FALL hazard on a mountain road, forcing major protective engineering

questions.question: Gabions are:
options: Wire baskets packed with rock, used to hold the toe of a slope where support was removed

questions.question: Managing water on a slope includes:
options: Discharging stormwater onto the slope face
Cut-off drains above the slope, subsurface drains bleeding water out, and fixing leaking pipes
Watering the slope in dry weather

questions.question: Vegetation protects a slope because:
options: It shades the rock from sunlight only
It attracts animals that compact the soil
Roots BIND the soil, plants intercept rain, and transpiration dries the slope

questions.question: Planning-level strategies include:
options: Building clinics on the steepest slopes
Ignoring hazard maps to save money
GIS hazard mapping, keeping housing off high-risk slopes, rainfall-triggered evacuation warnings and community education on warning signs

questions.question: The tug-of-war picture puts gravity against:
options: Friction, particle grip and plant roots stitching the soil like threads in fabric

questions.question: The sandcastle shows water's double role because:
options: DAMP sand glues grains together, but a poured bucket forces grains apart and slumps the castle into soup
Dry sand builds the best castles

questions.question: Cutting a platform, stripping grass and leaking pipe water onto one hillside means:
options: People have weakened the slope in three ways at once — less support, no roots, more water
Only earthquakes can now move the slope

subtopics.title: The Six Speeds of Falling Ground

questions.question: The six gears from slowest to fastest are:
options: Creep, solifluction, landslide, slump, rock fall, mud flow
Mud flow, rock fall, slump, landslide, solifluction, creep
Creep, rock fall, mud flow, slump, landslide, solifluction
Landslide, creep, slump, mud flow, solifluction, rock fall

questions.question: Tree trunks curved like bananas on a hillside are paperwork for:
options: SOIL CREEP — the trees keep growing upright while their bases slip slowly downhill

questions.question: The loaded tow truck losing its bakkie off the flatbed pictures:
options: A LANDSLIDE — one coherent mass letting go and sliding along a plane, usually after soaking rain

questions.question: The ladder's overall trend is:
options: All six move at the same speed
Speed UP, water UP — from slow dry creep to the fast fluid mud flow

subtopics.title: April 2022 and How to Fight Back

questions.question: The sentence that shows understanding of the 2022 Durban disaster is:
options: Same rain, unequal risk — the poorest households stood on the steepest, least engineered slopes when the hills gave way
The rain fell only on informal settlements
Mass movement cannot happen in cities
The disaster had no human dimension

questions.question: Chapman's Peak Drive's half-tunnel works by:
options: Letting falling rock FLY OVER the road and into the sea

questions.question: The four fight-back moves are:
options: ENGINEER the slope, DRAIN the water, PLANT the surface, PLAN where people live

questions.question: Community warning signs of a slope preparing to fail include:
options: Fresh cracks, leaning poles, doors that suddenly jam, and water seeping from a previously dry hillside
